basics.name: João Galego
basics.label: Head of AI
basics.summary: João Galego is Head of AI at [Critical Software](https://www.criticalsoftware.com/) and Invited Professor at [Instituto Superior de Economia e Gestão (ISEG)](https://iseg.ulisboa.pt). He majored in Physics at [Instituto Superior Técnico (IST)](https://tecnico.ulisboa.pt/) in Lisbon and obtained a postgraduate diploma in Forensic Studies from [Instituto Superior de Ciências Sociais (ISCSP)](https://www.iscsp.ulisboa.pt/). He did doctoral work in Cognitive Science at ULisboa, where he used machine learning (ML) to decode complex brain signals and study motor cognition. Prior to joining Critical Software, João served as Lead ML Engineer at Siemens and held roles as Solutions Architect, ML Specialist, and Quantum Ambassador at AWS. At Critical Software, his mission is to bring AI to high-stakes domains and build ML that matters. When he is not working or teaching, you can usually find him browsing local bookstores, contributing to open-source projects, or enjoying quality time with his family.

awards.title: IBM Quantum Challenge - Advanced, 1st Place
awards.summary: Space-themed, quantum computing hackathon organized by [IBM Quantum](https://quantum-computing.ibm.com/). Exercises included an exploration of primitives using the new [Qiskit Runtime](https://qiskit.org/documentation/partners/qiskit_ibm_runtime/), applying error mitigation techniques like [matrix-free measurement mitigation](https://github.com/Qiskit-Partners/mthree) (M3) to ML problems involving quantum kernels, implementing [problem-specific parameterized quantum circuits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.05643) to solve the traveling salesman problem, and the application of quantum chemistry techniques to study the [interstellar medium](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/chapterhtml/2017/bk9781782627760-00001?isbn=978-1-78262-776-0) by computing the reaction energy of H₃⁺, the first [excited state](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.08138) and dipole moment of C₃H₂ ([Cyclopropenylidene](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11542419/)), and the interstellar chain reaction energy of [C + C₂H₂ → C₃H₂](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jp020310z). For more information, check out the [official announcement](https://research.ibm.com/blog/quantum-challenge-fall-2022) on the IBM research blog.
